In /bench/repo (Go project, memos fork), answer with exact path:line citations:

(1) Webhook trace: find which gRPC/RPC handler methods (in server/router/api/v1/ or similar) can transitively cause an outbound HTTP request to a user-configured webhook URL. Trace from handlers like CreateMemo/UpdateMemo/DeleteMemo (and any comment/reaction handlers that call a webhook dispatch helper) to the single convergence function where all paths meet before delivery (e.g. a dispatchMemoRelatedWebhook helper and/or internal/webhook Post function). List at least 3 handler methods with path:line and the convergence function with path:line.

(2) Avatar trace: trace how a browser request for another user's profile image (avatar) reaches stored data. Find the HTTP/gRPC handler that serves avatars (search for "avatar" in server/router), then each hop: handler → store method (store/user.go) → driver implementation (store/db/sqlite/user.go etc.). Give each hop as: symbol — path:line.

Return concise findings.

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

content.text:
Findings.

## (1) Webhook trace — outbound HTTP to user-configured URLs

Handler entry points (all `APIV1Service`, exposed via Connect/gRPC in `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/connect_services.go`):

- `CreateMemo` — /bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:70 → calls `DispatchMemoCreatedWebhook` at /bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:157
- `UpdateMemo` — /bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:401 → `dispatchMemoUpdatedSideEffects` at /bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:513
- `DeleteMemo` — /bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:518 → `DispatchMemoDeletedWebhook` at /bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:562
- `CreateMemoComment` — /bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_comments.go:20 → `DispatchMemoCommentCreatedWebhook` at /bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_comments.go:119
- `SetMemoAttachments` — /bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_attachment_service.go:16 → `dispatchMemoUpdatedSideEffects` at /bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_attachment_service.go:48
- `SetMemoRelations` — /bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_relation_service.go:16 → `dispatchMemoUpdatedSideEffects` at /bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_relation_service.go:48

Reaction handlers (`UpsertMemoReaction` /bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/reaction_service.go:60, `DeleteMemoReaction` :111) do NOT reach webhooks — they only broadcast SSE.

Convergence chain:

- `dispatchMemoUpdatedSideEffects` — /bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_update_helpers.go:66 (shared fan-in for update/attachments/relations)
- Thin wrappers `DispatchMemoCreatedWebhook` / `DispatchMemoUpdatedWebhook` / `DispatchMemoDeletedWebhook` — /bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go:15, :20, :25
- **Convergence function: `dispatchMemoRelatedWebhook`** — /bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go:48. Loads user webhooks via `s.Store.GetUserWebhooks` (:57), sets `payload.URL = hook.Url` (:68) and enqueues `webhook.PostAsync(payload)` at /bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go:71. The comment path bypasses this function but converges at the same `webhook.PostAsync` call site style: /bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go:43.
- **Final egress: `webhook.PostAsync`** — /bench/repo/internal/webhook/webhook.go:184 (enqueues onto `asyncPostQueue`, cap 128, /bench/repo/internal/webhook/webhook.go:39) → 4 worker goroutines in `init()` at /bench/repo/internal/webhook/webhook.go:42-46 call **`webhook.Post`** — /bench/repo/internal/webhook/webhook.go:120, which builds the `http.NewRequest("POST", requestPayload.URL, ...)` (:126) and executes `safeClient.Do(req)` (/bench/repo/internal/webhook/webhook.go:152).

SSRF guard is at the transport layer: `safeDialContext` — /bench/repo/internal/webhook/webhook.go:59 (rejects private/reserved IPs at dial time), plus `ValidateURL` at write time in /bench/repo/internal/webhook/validate.go, used by `CreateUserWebhook` /bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/user_service_webhooks.go:74 and `UpdateUserWebhook` :161/:182.

## (2) Avatar trace — browser → stored data

- Route registration: `GET /file/users/:identifier/avatar` — /bench/repo/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:124
- `FileServerService.serveUserAvatar` — /bench/repo/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:168 (auth gate at :174 only when `!s.Profile.AllowAnonymous()`; identifier from path param at :183)
- `FileServerService.getUserByUsername` — /bench/repo/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:715 (`s.Store.GetUser(ctx, &store.FindUser{Username: &identifier})`)
- `Store.GetUser` — /bench/repo/store/user.go:148 (cache hit only when `find.ID != nil`, so username lookups always fall through)
- `Store.ListUsers` — /bench/repo/store/user.go:136 (delegates to `s.driver.ListUsers`, populates user cache)
- Driver: `(*DB).ListUsers` (sqlite) — /bench/repo/store/db/sqlite/user.go:88; username predicate at /bench/repo/store/db/sqlite/user.go:128; `AvatarURL` scanned at /bench/repo/store/db/sqlite/user.go:189. Parallel implementations: /bench/repo/store/db/mysql/user.go:84 and /bench/repo/store/db/postgres/user.go:87.
- Back in the handler: `parseDataURI` — /bench/repo/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:737 decodes the stored base64 data URI, MIME allowlist check against `avatarAllowedTypes` (/bench/repo/server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:75) at :201, then `c.Blob` at :208.

Related: the API converter rewrites base64 avatars to this `/file/{user}/avatar` URL — /bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/user_service_converters.go:36. Note the full `store.User` row (including `PasswordHash`) is loaded by this path, though only `AvatarURL` is emitted.
